extra.message: User input from request.GET['host'] is concatenated directly into a shell command string passed to os.system(). An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands (e.g., host=127.0.0.1;cat /etc/passwd).

User-controlled raw bytes (from request.body or request.GET['blob'], optionally base64-decoded) are passed to pickle.loads(), enabling arbitrary code execution. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload to execute any Python code on the server.

User input from request.GET['fragment'] is interpolated into a Jinja2 Template string which is then rendered and returned as HTML. This enables Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), allowing attackers to execute arbitrary Python code via Jinja2 payloads.

An lxml XMLParser is created with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, then used to parse user-supplied request.body. This configuration allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks, enabling file disclosure and server-side request forgery.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User-controlled JSON from request.body is used directly as a MongoDB query filter in find_one(). An attacker can pass MongoDB query operators (e.g., {"$gt": ""}) to manipulate the query and access unauthorized data.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: User input from request.GET['lane'] or request.POST['lane'] is passed directly to Django's redirect() without validation, allowing open redirect attacks. An attacker can craft URLs that redirect victims to malicious sites.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: User input from request.GET['ref'] is used directly in pathlib.Path construction (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json") without sanitization. An attacker can use path traversal sequences (e.g., ../../etc/cron.d/evil) to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The course_grade_file_094 view has no authentication check (_wrk_gate is not called). Any unauthenticated user can access this endpoint and retrieve sensitive operational information including payment flags and owner contact details.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The course_identity_ping_344 view has no authentication check (_wrk_gate is not called). Any unauthenticated user can access this endpoint and have their input reflected in the response, which could facilitate other attacks.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Hardcoded verifier values ("north": "4812", "south": "5930") are embedded in source code. These credentials cannot be rotated without changing the code and are visible to anyone with source access.

The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is set to the value of the request's Origin header, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to "true". This allows any origin to make authenticated cross-origin requests, effectively bypassing the same-origin policy.
The X-XSS-Protection header is explicitly set to "0" (disabled) and Content-Security-Policy is set to an empty string, removing browser-level XSS protections for this response.

A cookie is set using response.set_cookie() without Secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite flags. Additionally, user-controlled input (request.GET['marker']) is stored in the cookie without sanitization, potentially enabling XSS via cookie values.

A base workset dict with security-sensitive fields (role, approved, balance) is created and then updated with unvalidated user input via workset.update(payload). An attacker can override any field (e.g., {"role": "admin", "approved": true}) to escalate privileges.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: SSL certificate verification is explicitly disabled using ssl._create_unverified_context() when making an outbound HTTPS request. This allows man-in-the-middle attacks on the connection.
Environment variables (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE) and internal filesystem paths (BASE_EXPORT_DIR) are exposed in the JSON response, providing attackers with server configuration details.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Social Security Numbers and credit card numbers from request parameters are written to a file on disk and the file path is returned in the response. Sensitive PII/PCI data should never be stored in plaintext or accepted via GET parameters.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Authorization decision (elevated vs standard lane) is based on a client-controlled cookie (ops_badge) or header (x-ops-badge). An attacker can simply set the cookie or header to "lead" to gain elevated access.

The get_client_ip function blindly trusts the X-Forwarded-For header, which can be set by any client. This allows IP address spoofing, undermining the reliability of IP-based audit logging and any IP-based access controls.

The admin_user_toggle view performs a state-changing operation (enabling/disabling user accounts) via GET request without CSRF protection. Django's CSRF middleware only protects POST requests. An attacker can trick an admin into visiting a crafted URL to disable/enable arbitrary user accounts.

The assignment_status view changes assignment status via GET request without CSRF protection. An attacker can trick an authorized user into visiting a crafted URL to change assignment statuses (e.g., publishing drafts or archiving assignments).
The release_grade view releases grades to students via GET request without CSRF protection. An attacker can trick an instructor into visiting a crafted URL to prematurely release grades.

The request_resubmission view changes submission status via GET request without CSRF protection. An attacker can trick an instructor/TA into visiting a crafted URL to request resubmission on any submission.

The discussion_moderate view changes thread status (pin/lock/hide) via GET request without CSRF protection. An attacker can trick a moderator into visiting a crafted URL to change discussion thread statuses.

CSV user import uses a hardcoded default password "changeme123" when no password is provided in the CSV. This weak default may remain unchanged, leaving imported accounts vulnerable to brute-force attacks.

The file_download view has an authorization gap: (1) if resource.course is None (nullable field), any logged-in user can download the file regardless of ownership, and (2) teaching assistants are not checked at all — any TA can download any file with an associated course.

The SignUpForm includes a 'role' field with all role choices (including 'school_admin'). During signup, a user can select any role including school_admin, granting themselves full administrative privileges upon registration.

The Django SECRET_KEY has a hardcoded fallback value 'django-insecure-local-dev-only'. If the SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set, this known key is used, allowing session hijacking, CSRF token forgery, and other cryptographic attacks.

The DATABASE_URL has a hardcoded fallback containing database credentials (postgres://lms_user:lms_pass@localhost:5432/lms_db). If the environment variable is not set, these known credentials are used.
